questions.scenario: Two of your best friends are fighting over a misunderstanding and have stopped talking. What do you do?

options.text: Mediate the situation by talking to both, finding a compromise, and getting them to apologize.
Secretly figure out exactly who said what to whom to find the factual root cause of the fight.
Remind them of the 'friend group rules' and point out who is technically in the wrong.
Distract them by organizing a fun group outing to rebuild the positive vibe and make them forget the fight.

questions.scenario: You are assigned a group project with classmates you don't know well. How do you approach it?

options.text: Act as the unofficial leader who keeps everyone happy, resolves disagreements, and keeps communication flowing.
Observe everyone silently first to figure out their strengths so you know exactly who should do what.
Immediately set clear ground rules on deadlines, attendance, and fair workload distribution.
Start by breaking the ice, learning about their hobbies, and creating a fun team name to build camaraderie.

questions.scenario: When playing a competitive strategy board game (like Monopoly or Risk) with friends, your main strategy is...

options.text: Making alliances and negotiating clever trade deals with other players to protect yourself.
Tracking everyone's resources in your head and predicting their next moves before they make them.
Strictly enforcing the rulebook whenever someone tries to bend the rules or cheat.
Focusing on the theme, doing character voices, and just making sure everyone is having a great time.

questions.scenario: Your school is organizing a massive inter-school cultural fest. What role do you naturally take on?

options.text: Negotiating with the principal and teachers to get approvals for a larger budget and extended timings.
Analyzing past years' data to figure out which events attract the most crowd and make the most money.
Handling all the permissions, safety protocols, and ensuring no school policies are violated.
Reaching out to different clubs to ensure every art form, food, and culture is beautifully represented.

questions.scenario: You hear a damaging rumor spreading about someone in your class. How do you react?

options.text: Talk directly to the key people involved to clear the air peacefully before it turns into a massive drama.
Trace the rumor back to its original source to find out exactly who started it and what their motive was.
Report it to the class teacher or monitor because spreading false information is against school policy.
Change the subject loudly whenever it's brought up and spread positive news to shift the class's mood.

questions.scenario: Your family is planning an international vacation. What is your primary contribution?

options.text: Balancing everyone's opinions so both your parents and siblings get to visit the places they want.
Deeply researching the destination for hidden gems, local scams to avoid, and the most efficient routes.
Organizing the visas, double-checking the passports, and making sure all travel documents are flawless.
Learning a few phrases of the local language and looking up traditional street foods you absolutely must try.

questions.scenario: You are watching an intense debate competition at school. What impresses you the most?

options.text: How the speakers gracefully handle aggressive questions without losing their temper.
The hard statistics and undeniable facts they use to destroy their opponent's arguments.
Whether their arguments are logically sound, fair, and strictly follow the debate format.
The speakers' charisma, body language, and how emotionally they connect with the audience.

questions.scenario: A new exchange student from another country joins your class. How do you interact with them?

options.text: Introduce yourself warmly and offer to be their guide to help them navigate the confusing school system.
Notice small details like their accent, notebook brands, and habits to figure out more about their background.
Ensure the other students treat them fairly and step in immediately if someone makes an inappropriate joke.
Ask them all about their country's music and food, and eagerly share your favorite local snacks with them.

questions.scenario: You are watching a political thriller or spy movie. Which scene excites you the most?

options.text: The high-stakes negotiation scene where leaders prevent a war using just their words and leverage.
The surveillance scenes involving hacking, tracking targets, and piecing together classified information.
The intense courtroom drama or the moment a character finds a genius loophole in a treaty.
The glamorous embassy parties, diverse global locations, and characters speaking multiple languages.

questions.scenario: What is your preferred strategy to convince your parents to buy you something expensive?

options.text: Propose a win-win deal, like promising to take on extra chores or get certain grades in exchange.
Gather data on price comparisons, durability, and why it is a logical, long-term investment.
Bring up a past promise or condition they set, proving that you have technically fulfilled your end of the deal.
Show them a beautifully made video or tell an emotional story about how much joy and value it will bring.

Diplomat_Negotiator.title: Diplomat / Foreign Service Officer
Diplomat_Negotiator.primary_match_text: You are a natural peacemaker and negotiator. You excel at balancing different viewpoints, resolving conflicts calmly, and building strong relationships.
Diplomat_Negotiator.day_in_the_life: Representing your country at international summits, negotiating trade agreements, and managing crises at foreign embassies to maintain global peace.
Diplomat_Negotiator.alternative_match_text: Because you are great at managing people and expectations, roles in corporate public relations, human resources, or mediation are excellent backups.
Diplomat_Negotiator.roadmap: Take Humanities (Arts) or any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a Bachelor's degree (Political Science/History preferred), then crack the UPSC Civil Services Examination to join the Indian Foreign Service (IFS).

Intelligence_Analyst.title: Intelligence & Security Analyst
Intelligence_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are incredibly observant and analytical. You love connecting the dots, gathering information, and reading between the lines to uncover the truth.
Intelligence_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Analyzing global data, assessing security threats, decoding foreign communications, and advising government leaders on national security risks.
Intelligence_Analyst.alternative_match_text: With your sharp analytical mind, careers in cybersecurity, data analytics, or corporate risk management are highly lucrative and intellectually stimulating.
Intelligence_Analyst.roadmap: Take any stream (Science or Humanities preferred) in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Political Science, International Relations, or Cyber Security, followed by exams for intelligence agencies (like IB or RAW).

International_Lawyer.title: International Law Expert
International_Lawyer.primary_match_text: You have a strong sense of justice and rules. You believe in structure, fairness, and using legal frameworks to solve complex global problems.
International_Lawyer.day_in_the_life: Drafting international treaties, advising the government on maritime laws, or representing the country in human rights cases at the International Court of Justice.
International_Lawyer.alternative_match_text: Since you thrive on logic and rules, practicing corporate law, civil litigation, or working with global NGOs as a legal advisor are fantastic alternative paths.
International_Lawyer.roadmap: Take Humanities or Commerce in 11th/12th. Clear the CLAT exam to pursue a 5-year integrated law degree (BA LLB), and specialize in International Law or Human Rights.

Cultural_Ambassador.title: Public Diplomat / Cultural Attaché
Cultural_Ambassador.primary_match_text: You are a people person who loves diversity. You use art, language, culture, and communication to bridge the gap between different countries.
Cultural_Ambassador.day_in_the_life: Organizing massive international cultural festivals, running educational exchange programs, and using soft power to improve your country's global image.
Cultural_Ambassador.alternative_match_text: Because you are deeply empathetic and creative, working in international journalism, event management, or as a translator are exciting, travel-heavy careers.
Cultural_Ambassador.roadmap: Take Humanities in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Foreign Languages, Cultural Studies, or Mass Communication. Mastering 1-2 foreign languages (like French, Spanish, or Mandarin) is highly recommended.
